problem.title: Classic security tools are no longer enough on their own
problem.p1: The surface to protect has changed: dozens of SaaS tools wired into your data, coding agents opening pull requests, years of accumulated configs and permissions. Each tool sees its own slice; nobody sees the whole.
problem.p2: A one-off audit or a quarterly scan captures a state that drifts the very next day: a role widened “temporarily”, a dependency bumped, a bucket opened for a test. CTOs, CISOs and platform leads need a continuous loop, not one more report.
problem.p3: Recent incidents are a reminder: exposed secrets and legacy runtimes are still open doors. We broke them down in <link>Black October: what it means for AI agents</link>.

whatFor.q: What does Quivr do for me, in plain words?
whatFor.a: It keeps every article, email and post, even when a service goes down, and keeps the earlier version when one is corrected. It lets you search by meaning, not just keywords, and shows the exact passage. And it tells your app when a new article matches a topic you described, with the reason it matched.

underTheHood.a: A Go engine, one binary for the API, the worker and migrations, on PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage and Temporal. Search runs on Weaviate, by keyword and by vector, with multilingual E5 embeddings. It exposes an HTTP API (v0), signed webhooks, a change feed (polling or SSE) and MCP for AI agents.

v1.a: Quivr V2 replaced the V1 code base on the main branch. V1 is preserved at the v1-final tag, the last commit of Quivr V1, so you can still read, fork or run it from there.

license.a: MIT. It is free to use, modify and self-host. Some plugins rely on libraries with their own license, such as pypdf (BSD-3-Clause) for the PDF plugin.

production.q: Can I use Quivr V2 in production?
production.a: Not yet. Quivr V2 is at the evaluation stage and its API is v0, which may change without notice. Try it on your machine with the Quickstart, and talk to us if you want to plan a production rollout.

selfHost.a: Yes. Quivr runs on servers you control, next to your application: one machine with Docker Compose to evaluate it, or a deployment with separate workers and a dedicated vector host. By default, Quivr itself sends document text nowhere outside your installation.

support.a: For questions and bugs, use the issues and discussions of the GitHub repository. For business plugins, planning a production rollout, or hosting that works to HDS requirements for health data, The Vibe Company can help as a service: book a call.

problem.title: A POC doesn't die for lack of a model — it dies for lack of production
problem.p1: The demo works. Then the real questions arrive: which permissions the agent gets, on which tools (whose APIs change or go down), who owns it when it gets things wrong, and which metric says it is useful. With no answers, nobody dares let it act, and the pilot stays a pilot.
problem.p2: COOs, heads of support and product CTOs are not waiting for one more slide. They want a first agent that is useful in real conditions, wired into their systems, that their teams use every day.
problem.p3: New to the topic? Start with our <link>guide to AI agents for business</link>. This page is about deploying one with you.

run.title: Run and handoff
run.desc: Runbooks, training for your teams, or joint operation: the agent has an owner the day it goes to production.

offer.complement: Complementary to our <hardening>AI agents to harden your product and stack</hardening> (the security of your infrastructure) and to our article on <authority>agent authority</authority> (in French; what an agent is allowed to do).

method.title: From the demo to the daily run
method.intro: You don't go from POC to production in one leap. We widen the scope as trust builds, with the numbers to back it.

call.label: Call
call.title: A 30-minute call
call.desc: The candidate process, the tools in place, the level of risk. By the end of the call, you know whether a first agent holds up at your company.

scope.label: Scoping
scope.title: Fixed-scope framing
scope.desc: A single workflow, and measurable success criteria set before the first line is written.

pilot.label: Pilot
pilot.title: An instrumented pilot
pilot.desc: The agent runs in near-real conditions, often as drafts first: it proposes, your team decides.

scale.label: Scaling
scale.title: Widen once the numbers hold
scale.desc: We widen the scope only when human acceptance and the metrics hold up. Not before.

production.label: Production
production.title: Secure production
production.desc: Permissions reviewed, documentation up to date, and GDPR and HDS requirements met when the context calls for it.

handover.label: Handoff
handover.title: Handoff or joint run
handover.desc: Your team takes the agent over with runbooks and training, or we keep operating it alongside you.

method.ctaTitle: A POC gathering dust? We start from what exists and take it all the way to the daily run, with your teams.
method.checklist: The full checklist before going to production

proof.title: Agents already running in real conditions
proof.intro: Case studies published on this site, with their numbers. Nothing else.

cases.locservice: An agent drafts the reply to every ticket, connected to internal APIs, on hundreds of tickets a day. A human reviews and decides: the drafts are used on 87% of tickets.
cases.coup-de-pates: Quality-control AI skills that check product documents (labels, specifications) and flag every discrepancy, alongside Ensemble, the employee CSR app.
cases.theodo: Technical expert embedded in Theodo's teams: Software Factories for hundreds of developers, with standardized agents and skills.

chatbot.title: Not a generic chatbot
chatbot.desc: A chat with no tools and no context does not change how your teams work. Here, the agent is wired into your systems and has a precise role.

replace.title: Not “we replace your support team”
replace.desc: The agent takes the repetitive part. Your teams keep the decisions, the customer relationship and the hard cases.

hardening.title: Not our hardening offer
hardening.desc: Hardening secrets, IAM or CI with a fleet of agents is a different page.
hardening.link: AI agents to harden your product and stack

promise.title: Not a compliance or zero-error promise
promise.desc: An agent sometimes gets things wrong. We design it so the error shows, reaches a human and gets fixed, and we document what was done.

start.q: Which process should we start with?
start.a: A high-volume process, with fairly stable rules, where an agent's mistake stays contained. Often the agent starts by writing a draft rather than sending directly.

timeline.q: How long until an agent is useful?
timeline.a: We work in short cycles, and we won't give you a generic timeline before we have seen the process. On our published customer support case, the agent's drafts are used on 87% of tickets, out of several hundred tickets a day.

existing.q: What if we already have an in-house POC?
existing.a: We start from what exists: tools, prompts, and the authority debt that has piled up (what the agent can do without anyone having decided it). We industrialize rather than rewrite everything.

data.a: We work to GDPR and HDS requirements. When health data is involved, the agent runs inside the client's covered environment. We claim no certification we do not hold.

article.q: How is this different from your “AI agents for business” article?
article.a: The article explains what an agent is and how to get started. This page is the offer: we deploy the agent with you, all the way to production.

hardening.q: How does this relate to your AI agents for hardening?
hardening.a: Hardening is a fleet of agents that secures your product and your infrastructure. Here, these are business agents in production. The two often go together.
